text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The editorial says Fatos Nano's Socialist-led government passed the crucial international test when it received a letter from U.S. Presiden Bill Clinton supporting the coalition.
- The 7,000 soldiers of the Italian-led multinational protection force packed up camp after four months in troubled Albania.
- The state-owned Albanian radio and television nominated Albert Minga as its general director.
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) donated $10 million to help Albanian private business get back on its feet but it says it needs at least $20 million more.
- Four trucks transporting cigarettes broke through the border crossing point of Qafe e Thanes with Macedonia and shot at custom officials.
- Sali Berisha, former president and leader of the Democratic party, met four alliance parties to discuss strategies against the ruling Socialist party.

- Albanian Foreign Minister Paskal Milo met the Yugoslav ambassador to Tirana suggested dialogue should be resumed with Serbia to improve relations and the situation of ethnic Albanians in the Serbian province of Kosovo.
- Many ships are waiting to be unloaded in Durres port. The port has not been operating since March when the civil unrest started.
- Detlof von Berg of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said the organisation will decide on its further mandate in Albania on August 21.
- The Independent Trade Union, the biggest in the country, chose Xhevdet Lubani as its new leader after Valer Xheka resigned and left the country.
